result.title: From Outcomes to Components: A Counterfactual Evaluation Framework for LLM-Proposed Repairs
result.summary: An LLM-generated repair action specifies which records to change and by how much. A failed action may still contain a useful target set or numerical update, depending on how the two are paired. We evaluate this problem in traffic networks and databases, where aggregate observations obscure the records that need correction. We examine the pairings by executing each combination from the same initial state, using a reference action that restores the affected records. In 76 of 114 traffic actions, the gain from correcting both parts exceeds the sum of the gains from correcting each part alone. Six of these actions become worse after either correction alone, but improve when both parts are corrected. In database repair, replacing only the proposed update with the reference update worsens 17 of 108 model actions, all of which select unaffected records. We also test whether parts of two proposals can be reused. On held-out observations, selecting among the proposals and their recombined target-update pairs recovers 61.6% of the reference action's loss reduction, compared with 58.0% from selecting between the proposals alone.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出反事实评估框架，把 LLM 给出的修复动作拆成「目标记录集合」与「数值更新」两部分，在交通网络和数据库任务中从同一初始状态执行各种组合，量化两部分的因果贡献，并测试能否跨提案重组这些部分。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文属纯文本/结构化 LLM 工作、不含视觉，但其按组件做反事实拆分与贡献评估的思路，可能为 LVR 中 latent 内容与答案的贡献分配、轨迹监督提供可供核查的方法线索。
